title: 2027 Gaius Charles Bolin Dissertation and Post-MFA Fellowship: Economics
description:
2027 Gaius Charles Bolin Dissertation and Post-MFA Fellowship:
Economics
Williams College: Bolin Fellowship

Location: Williamstown, MA
Open Date: Sep 01, 2026
Deadline: Nov 15, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time

Description
The Gaius Charles Bolin Fellowships at Williams College are
designed to strengthen and expand the professoriate by supporting
scholars and artists whose research, teaching, and engagement
contribute to inclusive and intellectually vibrant academic
communities. Through sustained mentorship, professional
development, and full participation in the intellectual life of the
College, fellows are supported as they prepare for faculty careers.
Established in 1985, the program supports advanced graduate
students and post-MFA artists.

Gaius Charles Bolin was the first Black graduate of Williams in
1889. He was an active and influential member of his class who went
on to a successful career as a lawyer in Poughkeepsie, New York.
Bolin also was a founding member of the local branch of the NAACP
and was the first African American president of the Dutchess County
Bar Association. In 1969, eighty years after Gaius Bolin graduated,
Joseph E. Harris, the first Black tenure-line faculty member, was
hired at Williams.

In honoring this legacy, the fellowship supports scholars and
artists whose research, teaching, and creative work expand the
range of questions, perspectives, and communities represented in
academic scholarship, and who are prepared to contribute to
inclusive, rigorous, and collaborative academic environments.

The Bolin Fellowship is structured as a two-year residency at
Williams. Two scholars or artists are appointed each year. Fellows
devote the bulk of the first year to the completion of dissertation
work-or in the case of post-MFA applicants, building their
professional portfolios-while also teaching one course as a faculty
member in one of the college's academic departments or programs.
The second year of residency, preferably with a terminal degree in
hand, is spent on academic career development while again teaching
just one course. Through this structure, fellows gain experience as
teacher-scholars while advancing significant scholarly or creative
work.



Qualifications
The Bolin Fellowships are awarded to applicants who show
exceptional promise as scholars, who have an interest in and
capacity for teaching students in a community that is broadly
diverse across multiple dimensions, including race, gender,
citizenship, ethnicity, religion, and lived experience, and who are
pursuing a career in higher education in the United States.
Competitive applicants will demonstrate the ability to engage
diverse perspectives through their research, teaching, or creative
work, and to contribute to an inclusive academic environment.

Ph.D. candidates must have completed all doctoral work except the
dissertation by the end of the current academic year. Post-MFA
candidates must be recent recipients of the degree; only those with
degrees granted in 2026, or to be granted in 2027, are eligible to
apply.

The annual stipend for the position is $60,000. The College will
also provide health and dental benefits, relocation and housing
assistance, academic support including office space and a computer,
and an annual allowance of $4,000 for research-related
expenses.

During the period of residence at Williams, the Bolin Fellows will
be affiliated with an appropriate department or program and will be
expected to teach one one-semester course each year, normally in
the fall semester of year one and the spring semester of year two.
Fellows are also encouraged to participate in the broader
intellectual and community life of the College. Forms of
participation include programming within a fellow's affiliated
unit, attendance at First3 luncheons focused on scholars in their
first three years at the college, and events hosted by the Rice
Center for Teaching.



Application Instructions
Candidates should apply via Interfolio by 11:59pm on November 15,
2026, with:


a cover letter with a description of your research and teaching
interests; this letter should also explain how you will effectively
engage a broadly diverse student body and contribute to an academic
environment that values diverse perspectives and experiences
a full curriculum vitae
two confidential letters of recommendation, including one
letter of recommendation that addresses the applicant's ability to
contribute to inclusive academic environments and to advance
understanding of diverse perspectives and experiences
PhD applicants: a copy of the dissertation prospectus,
preferably limited to 10-15 pages, or a research statement of the
same length; and a timetable for completion of the degree
Post MFA applicants: project description, preferably limited to
2-5 pages [250-1250 words], and additional material, as described
below:


Writers: 2-3 short stories, 10-15 poems, or novel passages not
to exceed 50 pages
Visual Artists: 20 images
Theatre Artists: sample of design portfolio, links to
performances





Eligible candidates for the fellowship include all U.S. citizens,
U.S. nationals, and U.S. permanent residents (holders of a
Permanent Resident Card); individuals granted deferred action
status under the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals Program;
Indigenous individuals exercising rights associated with the Jay
Treaty of 1794; individuals granted Temporary Protected Status;
asylees; and refugees. Eligible candidates may apply to more than
one academic unit.

Units that will be participating in 2026-27 are:

Economics German Jewish Studies Math Philosophy Physics &

Williams College is a liberal arts institution located in the
Berkshire Hills of western Massachusetts. The college has built its
reputation on outstanding teaching and scholarship and on the
academic excellence of its approximately 2,000 students. Please
visit the Williams College website (http://www.williams.edu). Williams promotes equal
opportunity and makes all employment decisions on a non-discriminatory basis.
Williams College is committed to building a diverse and inclusive
community where individuals of all identities and backgrounds can
live, learn, and thrive.
